what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: Ask each funder's own page whether its fund is still open
agents.why: Ninety-odd funds are questionable: some look retired, some closed, and ninety-three are being held open by nothing more than the fact that we once saw money move. We will not decide any of that ourselves — the funder's own page decides, one row at a time, and the answer gets written down and kept. The last audit like this was never committed and had to be thrown away, which is the reason this one produces a file before it produces an opinion.

agents.what: Find funds a Norwegian founder can actually apply to
agents.why: Norway has nothing real in the corpus. Its research council re-booked its accounts onto new codes last year and we ingested the codes as if they were programmes, so a Norwegian founder is being shown bookkeeping. Finding a genuine source — the research council's own calls, Innovasjon Norge, Enova — is the difference between a market we serve and one we only appear to.

agents.what: Make the paid test ready to fire, and say honestly whether it can settle anything
agents.why: We are about to spend real money asking whether letting the model pick the five beats our own scoring. The last run of this kind was too small to tell a real difference from chance, and settled nothing. So this one is written down in advance — what would count as a win, what as a loss, what as inconclusive — and rehearsed without spending, before a cent goes out.
